Harbor root is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sailor/3ec38e8b-1ace-545e-a82a-ac4418d8c2a1/scratchpad/ref/harbor (v0.8.5, MIT). The paths below are relative to that root.

PLAYER ARCHITECTURE
- src/views/player.tsx (1323 lines) composes about 28 hooks from src/views/player/hooks/ on top of a PlayerBridge.
- PlayerBridge is defined in src/lib/player/bridge.ts:53-78. Methods: load, play, pause, seek, setVolume, setMuted, setRate, setAudioTrack, setSubtitleTrack, setSubDelay, setAudioDelay, addSubtitle(url, lang, title, select), setAudioNormalize, screenshot, setAbLoop, subscribe. Its PlayerSnapshot carries audioTracks, subtitleTracks, chapters, subDelaySec, audioDelaySec, subText, subStartSec, videoWidth and videoHeight.
- The mpv bridge is src/lib/player/mpv.ts. It invokes commands in src-tauri/src/mpv.rs, which always uses libmpv in-process:
  - mpv_start{args:{url, startAtSec, subtitles:[{url,lang}], anime4k, hdrToSdr, embed, anime4kShaders}}
  - mpv_command{cmd:[...]} — raw argv, no allow-list
  - mpv_set_property{name, value} — raw, no allow-list
  - mpv_sub_add{url, lang, title, select}
  - sub_download{url} returns a local path
  - mpv_set_geometry, mpv_stop
- Events arrive on Tauri event "mpv://event": {event:"property-change", name, data} | end-file{reason} | file-loaded | playback-restart | seek | log.
- Observed properties (mpv.rs:92-108): time-pos (throttled to 200 ms), duration, pause, eof-reached, track-list, volume, mute, chapter-list, sub-delay, audio-delay, sub-text, sub-start, af, dwidth, dheight.
- Playback position lives outside React state in src/lib/player/playback-clock.ts (useSyncExternalStore), so 200 ms ticks do not re-render menus.
- Harbor has no external-process mpv. Its non-embed mode is libmpv in its own window with ontop=yes.

(a) SKIP INTRO / RECAP / CREDITS — src/lib/skip-intro/
- aniskip.ts:
  - Converts kitsu:<id> to a MAL id via GET https://kitsu.io/api/edge/anime/{kitsuId}/mappings. It picks the data[] entry where attributes.externalSite == "myanimelist/anime" and takes attributes.externalId.
  - Then calls GET https://api.aniskip.com/v2/skip-times/{malId}/{episode}?types=op&types=ed&types=mixed-op&types=mixed-ed&types=recap&episodeLength={durationSec.toFixed(3)}.
  - Response: {found, results:[{interval:{startTime, endTime}, skipType}]}.
  - Mapping: op and mixed-op become intro, ed and mixed-ed become outro, recap becomes recap.
  - In-memory caches, including negative results.
- theintrodb.ts:
  - GET https://api.theintrodb.org/v2/media?tmdb_id=N or imdb_id=ttN, plus &season=S&episode=E.
  - Response: {tmdb_id, type, intro[], recap[], credits[], preview[]}, each entry {start_ms, end_ms}. A null start means 0; a null end means the duration.
  - credits and preview both map to outro. Used for tt and tmdb: ids, preferring episode.imdbId.
- chapters.ts classifies mpv chapter-list titles by regex:
  - recap: recap|previously
  - intro: opening|op|intro|opening credits|theme song
  - outro: ending|ed|outro|end/closing credits|credits
  - A segment ends at the next chapter's start (or at the duration, or start+90 s).
- index.ts:
  - useSkipSegments fetches only after durationSec > 0.
  - Priority is AniSkip, then IntroDB, then chapters. The first non-empty source wins; sources are not merged.
  - activeSegment matches when start <= pos < end - 0.75.
- UI: src/views/player/skip-pill-container.tsx and src/components/player/skip-pill.tsx.
  - A pill sits bottom-right (right-7, bottom-44) with a 200 ms fade and slide. Labels: Skip Intro / Skip Recap / Skip Credits.
  - An outro with a next episode shows "Next Episode".
  - In the last 15 s (UP_NEXT_WINDOW_SEC) an UpNextCard appears: still image, S/E label, "Up next in Ns", progress bar, Play now, and an X that cancels autoplay.
  - Synthetic outro: when a next episode exists and there is no real outro, the last 90 s count as an outro.
  - Skip seeks to endSec. The pill stays visible for the whole segment, but is hidden in PiP, draw mode and the resume prompt (player.tsx:1046-1059).
  - Harbor has NO auto-skip setting and NO skip hotkey (src/lib/hotkeys.ts).

(b) NEXT EPISODE
- src/views/player/hooks/use-episode-navigation.ts gets prev/next from src/lib/series-episodes.ts fetchAdjacentEpisodes (meta videos, the Kitsu addon for anime, TMDB seasons).
- It preloads both neighbours by re-running the whole stream pipeline in build-episode-player-src.ts: runPipeline, then resolve the top 6 candidates, then preflight. It swaps in the result with replacePlayerSrc, or falls back to openPicker(meta, ep, {autoPlay:true}).
- use-auto-next-episode.ts fires once per src.url when:
  - status is ended, or

- Harbor does NOT use Stremio's behaviorHints.bingeGroup for this. bingeGroup is parsed only for debrid cache flags (src/lib/streams/parser/parser-cache-flags.ts).
- Hotkeys: n/p and MediaTrackNext/MediaTrackPrevious.

(d) SUBTITLE SOURCES AND SWITCHING
- Stream-attached subtitles are added at load via sub_download + mpv_sub_add with select:false (mpv.ts:233-252).
- Providers in src/lib/subtitles/providers/:
  - opensubtitles-v3.ts: three hard-coded endpoints — opensubtitles.stremio.homes, opensubtitles-v3.strem.io, opensubtitles.strem.io. Request: GET {base}/subtitles/{movie|series}/{tt[:s:e]}.json. Response: {subtitles:[{id, url, lang, m?, SubFormat?, fps?, encoding?}]}, titled "OpenSubtitles V3 #n".
  - addons.ts: the user's addons that accept "subtitles". Request: GET {base}/subtitles/{type}/{id}[/videoHash=..&videoSize=..&filename=..].json.
  - wyzie.ts: https://sub.wyzie.io/search.
- search.ts:
  - Runs all providers with Promise.allSettled, then dedups by normalizeLang(lang)|url.
  - Buckets results per source. Within a bucket it sorts by:
    1. language preference rank
    2. streamMatchScore: release group +120, source token (bluray/web-dl/hdtv) +40, resolution +8, hearing-impaired -25
    3. downloads
    4. title
  - Buckets are then interleaved round-robin by source priority: opensubtitles 3, wyzie/jimaku 2, addon 1.
- language.ts: small ISO 639-2 to 639-1 table, normalizeLang, langScore, and pickBestTrack (skips forced tracks, prefers default).
- Autoload (src/views/player/hooks/use-track-autoload.ts):

  - Resolves the IMDb id and searches the preferred subtitle languages (Japanese is removed for non-anime).
  - Adds up to 6 subtitles per language (PER_LANG_MAX) with labels like "OpenSubtitles · release".
  - Selects the first one only if no preferred-language track is already selected.
  - Then picks the best audio and subtitle tracks by preference, with per-show prefs first.
- Download (mpv.rs:766-826 sub_download):
  - reqwest with a browser UA and a 15 s timeout; gunzip on the 1f8b magic bytes; extension from URL or content type.
  - Written to %TEMP%/harbor-subs/<uuid>.<ext>.
  - No size cap, no charset conversion, never cleaned up.
- mpv_sub_add (mpv.rs:719-764) runs: sub-add <path> select|auto <title> [<lang>].
- Menu (subtitle-menu.tsx, subtitle-menu/menu-body.tsx):
  - Off/On toggle and a language rail with flags and counts.
  - Tabs All / Embedded / External, HI and Forced chips, tags Forced / HI-SDH / Default / codec.
  - "Find more subtitles" search (search-section.tsx), a "Movie's too new" empty state (release under 14 days), and the DelayRow.
  - No local-file loading and no secondary subtitles.

BACKENDS
1) External mpv
- crates/zeiler-player/src/lib.rs Player::play (198-219) spawns mpv with build_mpv_args (69-92):
  - --force-window=immediate, --keep-open=yes, --playlist=-
  - plus --title, --force-media-title, --user-agent, --referrer, --http-header-fields-append, --start
- It writes the URL on stdin. There is no --input-ipc-server, so after launch Zeiler has no control and no telemetry: no position, tracks, subtitles or end-of-file.

- This is what src/views/PlayPicker.tsx play() (about lines 86-138) calls for both URL and torrent streams. PlayPicker never routes to the in-app player.

2) Embedded libmpv (cargo feature "embedded", Windows only)
- crates/zeiler-player/src/embedded.rs is an EmbeddedPlayer actor with commands Cmd::Load, SetProperty, Command, Quit.
- Init options: config=no, load-scripts=no, ytdl=no, osc=no, input-default-bindings=no, idle, keep-open, vo=gpu-next, hwdec=auto-safe, wid.
- OBSERVED (34-50): time-pos, duration, pause, paused-for-cache, cache-buffering-state, eof-reached, seeking, volume, mute, media-title, track-list, chapter-list, aid, sid, vid. track-list and chapter-list are observed as JSON strings, because libmpv2 6 has no node format.
- Events go out as "player://event": {type: property | start-file | file-loaded | seek | playback-restart | end-file{reason} | error | shutdown}.
- load() (292-318) sets headers via change-list, user-agent, referrer, start, force-media-title, then loadfile replace and pause=false. It does nothing with subtitles.
- Shell src-tauri/src/commands/mpv.rs:

  - player_embedded_set_property with PROPERTY_ALLOW (lines 93-105): pause, volume, mute, speed, aid, sid, vid, sub-delay, audio-delay, sub-scale, sub-pos

DEPENDENCIES
- The workspace tokio lacks the "net" feature, which named pipes and Unix sockets need.
- chardetng 1.0.0, encoding_rs 0.8.42 and flate2 1.1.10 are already in Cargo.lock (transitive).
- No tauri-plugin-dialog.
- The engine already re-targets a known infoHash to a new fileIdx (crates/zeiler-engine/src/engine.rs:265 update_only_files).
gaps: The external-mpv backend has no JSON IPC. Every in-player feature (tracks, subtitles, skip, next episode, delays, style) is impossible on the default path, and on Linux/macOS (where embedded is stubbed) it is the only path.

PlayPicker calls player_play (external, fire-and-forget) and never opens the #/player route. The route carries no meta/video/stream context (type, metaId, videoId, season/episode, transportUrl, bingeGroup, filename, videoHash/videoSize, stream.subtitles).
The embedded shell cannot load into a running core: player_embedded_start always respawns. Next episode and stream switch need a load-in-place command.
There is no get-property path in either backend, so a stats overlay or probing mpv capabilities is impossible.
Observed properties lack sub-delay, audio-delay, speed, secondary-sid and chapter. MpvTrack lacks external, external-filename, forced, hearing-impaired, codec-desc and demux-channels.

Subtitles: no subtitles_get fan-out or command; stream-attached subtitles are dropped; no download, size cap, gunzip or charset normalization; no sub-add path; no local-file loading; no addon or embedded language ranking or dedup; no auto-select by language preference.
No built-in subtitle addon. CONTRIBUTING.md currently permits metadata-only built-ins, so shipping OpenSubtitles v3 needs a policy wording change.
No subtitle style settings, no live in-player style panel, no delay UI or hotkeys, no encoding override (matters for Arabic windows-1256, Cyrillic windows-1251, etc.).
No skip-segment sources (AniSkip, TheIntroDB, chapter titles), no Rust command (CSP blocks webview fetch), no skip pill or Up Next card, no auto-skip settings. Harbor has no auto-skip either.
No next-episode computation from meta.videos, no bingeGroup matching, no prefetch, no auto-advance or countdown, no handoff back to PlayPicker for the next video.
Audio: no delay, normalization, volume above 100% or speed control. Track labels are minimal (no channel layout or default/forced flags).
Quality: no in-player stream switcher (reload at the current position), no HLS variant exposure, no stats overlay, no chapter ticks.
No per-show preferences (audio language, subtitle language, subtitle delay, rate).
Player.tsx re-renders the whole page on every 200 ms time-pos event, so there is no isolated position store like Harbor's playback-clock.

implementation_plan.details:
Move PlayerEvent out of embedded.rs into lib.rs (not feature-gated) so both backends emit the same shape, and add a variant ClientMessage { args: Vec<String> }.

Add one backend-neutral session type: `enum Session { Embedded(EmbeddedPlayer), External(ExternalIpcPlayer) }`. Its methods:
- load(PlaybackRequest)
- set_property(name, Value)
- command(Vec<String>)
- get_property(name) -> oneshot Result<Value>
- quit()

In the embedded actor, add Cmd::GetProperty(String, oneshot::Sender<Result<Value, String>>): read with mpv.get_property::<String> and parse JSON for list props, or f64/bool by a type table.

Extend OBSERVED in both backends with: sub-delay, audio-delay, speed, secondary-sid, chapter, demuxer-cache-time, dwidth, dheight.

Extend PlaybackRequest with `options: Vec<(String,String)>`. These are validated pre-load options set by the shell from settings (alang, slang, volume-max), never by the UI.

New file crates/zeiler-player/src/external_ipc.rs.

Spawn the located binary with:
- `--input-ipc-server=<endpoint>`. On Windows: \\.\pipe\zeiler-mpv-<uuid v4>. On Unix: <cache_dir>/ipc/mpv-<uuid>.sock inside a 0700 directory.
- `--idle=yes --keep-open=yes --force-window=immediate --title=Zeiler`.
- Keep the user's mpv config (unlike embedded config=no), but never pass the URL or headers on argv.

Connect with retry, up to 50 attempts every 100 ms:
- Windows: tokio::net::windows::named_pipe::ClientOptions::open; retry on NotFound or ERROR_PIPE_BUSY.
- Unix: tokio::net::UnixStream::connect.
- Requires adding "net" to the workspace tokio features.

Writer task sends newline-delimited `{"command":[...],"request_id":n}`.

Reader task parses each line as serde_json::Value:
- A `request_id` resolves a pending oneshot. error == "success" gives Ok(data); anything else gives Err(error).
- An `event` maps to PlayerEvent:
  - property-change{name,data} becomes Property. data is real JSON, so track-list arrives as an array.
  - start-file, file-loaded, seek, playback-restart and shutdown map one-to-one.
  - end-file{reason, file_error?} becomes EndFile, plus Error when reason is error.
  - client-message{args} becomes ClientMessage.
- Throttle time-pos to 200 ms, as in embedded.

After connecting:
- Send observe_property for every OBSERVED entry, using the index as the id.
- Set headers via ["change-list","http-header-fields","clr",""] and then append. This removes the documented argv-headers limitation.
- Send user-agent and referrer, then ["loadfile", url, "replace"].
- To start at an offset, set the `start` property first and use plain loadfile replace. The per-file option syntax of loadfile changed across mpv versions (the index argument).

Watch the child process and emit Shutdown on exit. Keep the old stdin-launch Player::play as a fallback only if the IPC connection never comes up.

Add unit tests for line framing and event mapping, using fixture strings that run on Linux.

implementation_plan.step: 3. Unified, validated player IPC in the Tauri shell
implementation_plan.details:
Replace the embedded-only commands with backend-neutral ones in src-tauri/src/commands/mpv.rs or a new playback.rs. Keep the old player_embedded_* names as thin aliases until Player.tsx migrates.

Commands, all emitting "player://event":
- player_start{request, backend:"auto"|"embedded"|"external"}: auto means embedded if available, otherwise external IPC.
- player_load{request}: load into the same core.
- player_stop
- player_set_property{name,value}
- player_command{args}
- player_get_property{name}: read allow-list only: video-codec, audio-codec, hwdec-current, estimated-vf-fps, container-fps, video-bitrate, audio-bitrate, frame-drop-count, vo-drop-frame-count, demuxer-cache-duration, cache-speed, mpv-version.

Use a table-driven validate_property(name, &Value):
- Booleans: pause, mute, sub-visibility, secondary-sub-visibility, sub-bold.
- Numeric ranges:
  - sub-delay and audio-delay: -600..600
  - speed: 0.25..4
  - sub-pos: 0..150
  - sub-scale: 0.3..3
  - sub-font-size: 10..120
  - sub-margin-y: 0..200
  - sub-border-size, sub-outline-size, sub-shadow-offset: 0..10
  - volume: 0..volume-max
- Colors must match ^#([0-9A-Fa-f]{6}|[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})$.
- Enums:
  - sub-ass-override: no|yes|scale|force|strip
  - sub-align-x: left|center|right
  - sub-align-y: top|center|bottom
  - sub-border-style: outline-and-shadow|opaque-box|background-box
- Track ids (aid, sid, vid, secondary-sid) must be an integer or no/auto.
- sub-font must come from a fixed list.

Add to COMMAND_ALLOW only sub-remove <int> and sub-reload <int>.

Never expose raw sub-add, loadfile, af, vf, glsl-shaders, run, script-message, keybind or define-section to the UI. Those are issued only by the dedicated commands in steps 4, 10 and 12.

(a) Fan-out. Add aggregate_subtitles(client, addons, type, video_id, extra, timeout) -> Vec<AddonSubtitles{transportUrl, addonName, subtitles, error}> in zeiler-addon/src/fanout.rs, mirroring aggregate_streams. Expose command subtitles_get{type, id, videoHash?, videoSize?, filename?} in commands/content.rs with a 10 s per-addon timeout. Extras use the existing ExtraValue/request.rs encoding: /subtitles/{type}/{videoId}/videoHash=..&videoSize=..&filename=...json.

(b) Fetch and normalize. New zeiler-addon/src/subfile.rs with fetch_subtitle(client, url, encoding_override) -> SubtitleFile{utf8_bytes, format: Srt|Vtt|Ass, detected_encoding}:
- http/https only.
- Streamed size cap of 10 MiB, like get_json.
- Gunzip on the 1f8b magic bytes (flate2).
- Reject zip and rar (PK\x03\x04, Rar!) with a clear error.
- Strip UTF-8 BOM and decode UTF-16 by BOM.
- If the bytes are not valid UTF-8, detect with chardetng::EncodingDetector (guess(None, true)) and decode with encoding_rs. encoding_override comes from encoding_rs::Encoding::for_label.
- Sniff format: WEBVTT means vtt, [Script Info] means ass, otherwise srt.

(c) Add to player. player_subtitle_add{url, lang?, label?, select, encoding?}:
- Fetch, then write <cache_dir>/subs/<uuid>.<ext>.
- Run sub-add <path> select|auto <title> <lang> on the active backend.
- Return {path, format, encoding}. The UI maps this to the new track via track-list external-filename.
- Purge <cache_dir>/subs on player_stop and at startup.

(d) Local files.
- player_subtitle_pick_local opens a file dialog from Rust with tauri-plugin-dialog (blocking_pick_file, filters srt/ass/ssa/vtt). Grant no JS permission. Read up to 10 MiB, apply the same normalization, then sub-add select.
- Also handle WindowEvent::DragDrop in Rust while a session is active, with an extension allow-list.

(e) Built-in subtitle addon. This depends on the built-in essential addons area. Snapshot the official https://opensubtitles-v3.strem.io/manifest.json into src-tauri/builtin/ like Cinemeta, flag it official+protected, add setting builtinOpensubtitles (default true), and prepend it in effective_addons(). Do NOT copy Harbor's mirror list (opensubtitles.stremio.homes) or Wyzie.

(f) Phase 2: compute the OpenSubtitles hash in Rust when the stream lacks one. The hash is file size plus the wrapping sum of 64-bit little-endian words over the first and last 64 KiB, fetched with two Range GETs (works against the engine loopback URL).

Create src/lib/subtitles.ts, adapted from Harbor src/lib/subtitles/search.ts and language.ts with an MIT header.

Language handling:
- normalizeLang with a full ISO 639-1 / 639-2 B and T table, plus OpenSubtitles specials (pob or pt-br map to pt-BR) and BCP-47 heads.
- languageName via Intl.DisplayNames.

Candidates:
- stream.subtitles, with source "stream"
- per-addon groups from subtitles_get

Dedup by normLang|url, then by id.

Ranking, in order:
1. Language preference rank.
2. Source priority: stream, then built-in OSv3, then other addons.
3. Release match against behaviorHints.filename, using Harbor's streamMatchScore: release group +120, source token +40, resolution +8, hearing-impaired -25.

Label each entry as `${label ?? addonName} #n`.

Auto-load at file-loaded:
- If mpv already selected a non-forced embedded track in a preferred language, keep it.
- Otherwise download and select the top candidate of the first preferred language.
- Pre-add autoAddPerLang (default 2; Harbor uses 6) unselected per preferred language.
- Everything else stays a lazy menu entry, downloaded on click.
- Fetch the subtitle list in parallel with loading, but call sub-add only after file-loaded. sub-add needs a loaded file, and external subtitles are dropped on the next loadfile.

Anime:
- Detect via kitsu:/mal: ids, type anime, or genre Anime.
- Use animeAudioLangs and keep Japanese in the lists. For non-anime, strip Japanese as Harbor does.

Create src/pages/player/SubtitleMenu.tsx, adapting Harbor subtitle-menu.tsx and subtitle-menu/{menu-body,delay-row,utils}.tsx to Zeiler tokens with an MIT header.

Contents:
- Off/On toggle.
- Language rail with preferred languages first and counts.
- Variant list with tabs All / Embedded / Addons / Local and HI / Forced chips.
- Tags: Forced, SDH, Default, codec, source addon.
- Lazy entries show a download spinner.
- "Load from file..." calls player_subtitle_pick_local.
- "Encoding" re-adds the same URL with an override: Auto, UTF-8, windows-1256, windows-1251, windows-1252, ISO-8859-2/7/8/9, GB18030, Big5, Shift_JIS, EUC-KR.
- DelayRow: -0.5 / -0.1 / +0.1 / +0.5 / reset, plus hotkeys z/x.
- Optional secondary subtitle picker setting secondary-sid.
- Quick style panel (size, position, background) that calls player_set_sub_style live and persists.

Hotkeys: s and c run `cycle sub`.

The menu works identically for both backends because every action goes through IPC.

Rust Settings (TS mirror in src/lib/types.ts) gains:
- `subtitles: { langs: Vec<String> (default derived from OS locale, else ["en"]), autoLoad: true, autoAddPerLang: 2, style: SubtitleStyle }`
- `audio: { langs: [], animeLangs: ["ja"], normalize: false, volumeMax: 200 }`

SubtitleStyle fields are all Option, so unset means mpv's default: fontSize, scale, color, outlineColor, outlineSize, backColor, borderStyle, shadowOffset, shadowColor, marginY, pos, alignX, alignY, bold, font, assOverride.

player_apply_preferences runs in Rust after every session start:
- Sets alang and slang, passing both 2- and 3-letter forms.
- Sets only the style fields that are Some. Failures are logged, not fatal.
- For outline, tries sub-outline-* first, then falls back to sub-border-*.
- Sets volume-max.

Keep mpv/libass rendering. Do NOT copy Harbor's sub-visibility=no plus HTML overlay: it cannot work for the external window and it destroys ASS typesetting. Leave assOverride unset by default, with a "Force my style on styled (ASS) subtitles" toggle that sets force.

Settings view gets a "Subtitles" card in the Player section with a preview, modeled on Harbor subtitle-section.tsx.

Per-show prefs:
- New data/player-prefs.json, LRU of 200 (Harbor player-prefs.ts semantics), held in AppState.
- Commands: player_prefs_get{metaId}, player_prefs_set{metaId, patch:{audioLang, subLang, subSource, subDelaySec, rate}}.
- Applied after file-loaded; written when the user picks something.

Create src/lib/play-context.ts as a module-level store. PlayPicker sets it before navigating to `#/player?type=..&metaId=..&videoId=..`. It holds:
- meta: type, id, name, poster, videos
- video: id, season, episode, title, thumbnail
- stream: behaviorHints including bingeGroup, filename, videoHash, videoSize; plus subtitles
- transportUrl and addonName
- pendingPicker, used by App on remount for the no-binge-match fallback

The hash keeps a minimal fallback for reloads and dev autoplay.

PlayPicker.play() switches from playerPlay to the player route for URL and torrent streams. Keep "Open in external mpv" as an explicit secondary action.

The embedded-player rollout itself belongs to the built-in player area; this step is the minimum the in-player features need.

New crate crates/zeiler-skip, with no tauri dependency, using reqwest + serde with JSON-fixture tests. It ports Harbor src/lib/skip-intro/aniskip.ts and theintrodb.ts (MIT notice).

API: SkipClient::segments(SkipQuery{meta_id, video_id, season, episode, duration_sec}) -> Vec<SkipSegment{kind: Intro|Recap|Outro, start_sec, end_sec, source: AniSkip|IntroDb}>.

ID routing:
- kitsu:<id>[:<ep>]: Kitsu mappings, then MAL id, then AniSkip with episode = ep.
- mal:<id>: AniSkip directly.
- tt<id>, with season/episode parsed from the video id tt..:S:E: TheIntroDB imdb_id.
- tmdb:...: TheIntroDB tmdb_id.

Use AniSkip first, and TheIntroDB only if AniSkip is empty.

Validation:
- Drop segments where end <= start or start >= duration; clamp to the duration.
- An IntroDB null start becomes 0; a null end becomes the duration.

LRU caches, including negative results. 8 s timeouts. UA Zeiler/<version>.

Command skip_segments_get{type, metaId, videoId, season?, episode?, durationSec} in src-tauri/src/commands/skip.rs, gated by settings.skip.onlineLookup.

On the TS side, src/lib/skip.ts holds the chapter classifier and activeSegment (start <= pos < end - 0.75), ported from Harbor chapters.ts/index.ts, plus the priority order aniskip, introdb, chapters. Call the command once per file when duration > 0 first arrives.

implementation_plan.step: 10. Skip pill, Up Next card and auto-skip
implementation_plan.details:
Create src/pages/player/SkipPill.tsx and UpNextCard.tsx, adapted from Harbor skip-pill.tsx and skip-pill-container.tsx:
- Same labels.
- 15 s Up Next window with countdown, progress bar, Play now and cancel.
- Synthetic 90 s outro only when a next episode exists and there is no real outro.
- Skip seeks to endSec. Enter triggers the visible pill when no menu is open.

New settings: `skip: { showButton: true, autoSkipIntro: false, autoSkipRecap: false, autoSkipCredits: false, onlineLookup: true }`.

Auto-skip rules:
- Fires once per segment per file.
- Only when position enters [start, start+2s) during normal playback, not after a user seek into the segment.
- Only for AniSkip/IntroDB segments or exact chapter matches, never for the synthetic outro.
- Shows a "Skipped intro - Undo" toast for 5 s. Undo seeks back and suppresses that segment.
- Auto-skipping credits goes to the next episode when one exists.

External backend:
- Same logic, driven by IPC events.
- Also prompt inside the mpv window via a dedicated Rust command player_osd_prompt{kind}. It sends `show-text "Skip intro - press Enter" 3000` and a temporary binding: `keybind ENTER "script-message zeiler-skip"` on mpv versions that have keybind, else `define-section zeiler-skip "ENTER script-message zeiler-skip" force` plus `enable-section`.
- The binding fires a client-message event, which maps to the skip action. Remove the binding when the segment ends.

implementation_plan.step: 11. Next episode / binge via Stremio bingeGroup
implementation_plan.details:
Create src/lib/next-video.ts.

Computing the next video:
- Sort meta.videos by (season, episode, released) and take the one after the current id.
- Skip season 0 specials unless the current video is itself a special.

Prefetch at remaining <= 90 s or at outro start:
- Call streams_get(type, next.id).
- The candidate is a stream from the same transportUrl whose behaviorHints.bingeGroup equals the current, non-empty bingeGroup.

On Next, or auto-advance (eof per Harbor's use-auto-next-episode rule, or the countdown ending):
- URL candidate: call player_load in the same core.
- Torrent candidate: call engine_resolve, then load. The engine already re-targets the same infoHash via update_only_files.
- If the infoHash changed, call engine_remove on the previous one when deleteOnStop is set.
- Reset per-file state: subtitles, skip, prefs.
- No candidate: leave the player and open PlayPicker for the next video through play-context.pendingPicker. This matches Stremio's behavior.

Settings: bingeWatching (auto-play next, default true), upNextSeconds (15).

Hotkeys: n/p and MediaTrackNext/MediaTrackPrevious.

Audio: src/pages/player/AudioMenu.tsx, adapted from Harbor audio-menu.tsx.
- Labels from track-list: language via Intl.DisplayNames, title, codec, demux-channel-count mapped to Stereo / 5.1 / 7.1, and Default / External flags.
- Audio-delay row.
- "Normalize volume" calls player_set_audio_normalize{on}. Rust sets a fixed `af` value (lavfi dynaudnorm=f=200:g=15:m=10:r=0.6), never a UI-supplied filter.
- volume-max 200, so the slider reaches 200%.

Speed menu: 0.5x to 2x via `speed`.

Quality means switching streams:
- An in-player Streams panel reuses PlayPicker rows from the cached streams_get result.
- Choosing one calls player_load with startAtSec = the current position when it is over 5 s (Harbor's use-stream-switcher rule).
- HLS variants: when track-list has more than one video track, show a Video/Quality menu on vid with demux-h. Verify per stream how mpv's demuxer exposes variants.

Stats overlay (key i) uses the player_get_property read allow-list.

Chapter ticks on the SeekBar come from chapter-list.

Split src/pages/Player.tsx into src/pages/player/*:
- usePlayerSession: backend selection, event subscription, reducer extended with the new properties and track fields.
- A playback-clock store adapted from Harbor src/lib/player/playback-clock.ts, so 200 ms time-pos updates only re-render the seek bar, pill and countdown.
- Menus.

The "external" phase becomes a full remote-control UI: all menus, skip and next work over IPC. A note says the video is in the mpv window, and a "Bring mpv to front" action is available.

Extend the MpvTrack type in src/lib/player-ipc.ts with external, external-filename, forced, hearing-impaired, codec-desc and demux-channels.

Update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:
- IPC surface: player_start/load/stop/set_property/command/get_property, player_subtitle_add, player_subtitle_pick_local, subtitles_get, skip_segments_get, player_prefs_*.
- Security: allow-lists, external IPC endpoint, subtitle download caps.
- Milestones.

CONTRIBUTING.md: change the wording to "metadata or subtitles only, switchable" built-ins.

THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md: list the Harbor-adapted files (skip-intro, subtitle ranking, menus, playback-clock), each keeping Harbor's MIT notice in its header.

README: feature list, and privacy disclosure for the AniSkip / TheIntroDB / Kitsu lookups.

risks:
External mpv JSON IPC varies by mpv version and by the user's config/scripts:
- keybind may be absent on older builds (needs a define-section fallback).
- sub-outline-* vs sub-border-* and sub-border-style differ by version.
- loadfile per-file option syntax changed.
Treat every property set as non-fatal and probe mpv-version before using version-specific commands. These version boundaries are from memory and should be verified against the bundled libmpv and common distro mpv builds.

IPC endpoint exposure:
- mpv JSON IPC accepts `run` (arbitrary process launch) from any client that can write to the pipe/socket.
- Mitigations: random names, a 0700 socket directory on Unix, and never observing path or stream-open-filename (loopback engine credentials and debrid URLs).
- Windows named-pipe default DACLs may grant read access more broadly. Verify, and consider having Zeiler create the pipe policy or connect immediately.

Expanding the property/command allow-lists widens the attack surface for addon-controlled strings:
- sub-add, loadfile, af, vf and glsl-shaders must stay behind dedicated Rust commands with validated inputs.
- Subtitle titles and labels from addons go through argv only, never a shell.

Content-neutral policy:
- A built-in OpenSubtitles v3 addon contradicts the current CONTRIBUTING.md wording (metadata-only) until it is amended.
- Do not copy Harbor's hard-coded OSv3 mirror (opensubtitles.stremio.homes) or the Wyzie aggregator.

Third-party skip services (AniSkip, Kitsu, TheIntroDB):
- Availability, rate limits and terms are unverified. Kitsu may have moved hosts (kitsu.io vs kitsu.app; the client follows redirects).
- Requests reveal what the user watches, so a settings toggle and disclosure are needed.
- Never block playback on these lookups; cache negatives.
- None of the API shapes could be live-verified here (the container proxy returned 403). They come from Harbor's parsers.

Auto-skip false positives:
- Chapter regexes such as \bop\b, \bed\b and 'credits' can misfire, and AniSkip segments can be submitted for a different cut.
- Mitigations: auto-skip off by default, only on high-confidence sources, and an Undo toast.

bingeGroup coverage is inconsistent across addons, and many set none. The fallback to the picker must be smooth.
- Torrent season packs rely on engine update_only_files.
- The deleteOnStop semantics when switching infoHash must not delete the next episode's data.

Encoding detection on short or ambiguous subtitle files can guess wrong. The manual encoding override in the menu is the escape hatch.
- Right-to-left scripts (Arabic) depend on the libmpv build having fribidi/harfbuzz, and on fonts with Arabic coverage.
Forcing ASS style overrides (Harbor's default 'force') breaks anime typesetting. Zeiler should keep mpv's default and make force opt-in.

Scope dependency on the built-in player area:
- The in-player features need PlayPicker to route into #/player with a play context.
- The embedded backend is Windows-only today, so on Linux/macOS everything depends on the new external IPC backend.
- Route handoff back to App (pendingPicker) crosses the separate React roots in main.tsx.
Performance: time-pos at 200 ms re-rendering the full Player page. Mitigate with a playback-clock store.

external_services.name: AniSkip API v2
external_services.shapes: { found: boolean, results: [ { interval: { startTime: number, endTime: number }, skipType: 'op'|'ed'|'mixed-op'|'mixed-ed'|'recap', ... } ] }. Mapping: op/mixed-op to intro, ed/mixed-ed to outro, recap to recap.
external_services.notes: Shape taken from Harbor src/lib/skip-intro/aniskip.ts; not live-verified (proxy 403). Needs a MAL id. Call only after duration is known. Treat non-2xx or found:false as empty and cache it.

external_services.name: Kitsu mappings (kitsu to MAL)
external_services.notes: Used only to turn kitsu: ids (anime-kitsu addon) into MAL ids. Cache permanently. Host may redirect to kitsu.app (unverified).

external_services.name: TheIntroDB v2
external_services.shapes: { tmdb_id, type, intro: [{start_ms|null, end_ms|null}], recap: [...], credits: [...], preview: [...] }. A null start becomes 0; a null end becomes the duration. credits and preview map to outro.
external_services.notes: Shape taken from Harbor src/lib/skip-intro/theintrodb.ts; not live-verified. Terms and rate limits unknown, so check before shipping.

external_services.name: OpenSubtitles v3 Stremio addon (official)
external_services.shapes: { subtitles: [ { id, url, lang (ISO 639-2, e.g. 'eng'), m?, SubFormat?, fps?, encoding? } ] }. Zeiler's Subtitle struct keeps id/url/lang/label and ignores the rest.
external_services.notes: Standard Stremio subtitles resource, so it goes through the existing AddonClient::subtitles plus a new aggregate_subtitles fan-out. Built in as a switchable subtitle-only addon (built-in addons area). Do not use Harbor's extra mirrors.

harbor_files_to_adapt.why: Port to Rust (crates/zeiler-skip/src/aniskip.rs): Kitsu-to-MAL mapping, AniSkip request params, skipType mapping, negative caching.
Port to Rust (crates/zeiler-skip/src/introdb.rs): id routing, null start/end handling, credits/preview mapped to outro.
Chapter-title classifier regexes, reused in src/lib/skip.ts.
Source priority (aniskip > introdb > chapters), fetch-after-duration rule, activeSegment end guard of 0.75 s.
Skip pill and UpNextCard layout, labels, 15 s countdown, cancel-autoplay, transitions.
Synthetic 90 s outro rule and remaining-time wiring.
End-of-episode detection (ended, error near end, stopped near end; once per URL).
Dedup key, per-source buckets, language rank, streamMatchScore and interleaving, ported to src/lib/subtitles.ts.
normalizeLang/langScore/pickBestTrack semantics; extend to the full ISO table.
Stremio subtitles URL shape with videoHash/videoSize/filename extras. Implement in the Rust fan-out instead.
Autoload policy: keep a selected preferred-language track, per-language cap, labels, per-show prefs first, Japanese stripped for non-anime.
Menu structure: Off/On, language rail, Embedded/External tabs, HI/Forced chips, tags, empty states.
Delay stepper UX (±0.1/±0.5/reset).
Audio track rows (language, codec, channels) and audio-delay row.
Per-show prefs fields and LRU-200 semantics, moved to a Rust-persisted player-prefs.json.
Mapping of style settings to mpv sub-* properties (extend with back-color, shadow, align-y, bold, font).
Settings card layout with live preview, reset-to-defaults and colour pickers.
sub_download (766-826) and mpv_sub_add (719-764) as the starting point for Zeiler's player_subtitle_add. Add http(s) check, size cap, charset normalization and a cache-dir cleanup.
useSyncExternalStore position store so 200 ms ticks do not re-render the whole player.
Stream switching that resumes at the current position (>5 s rule).
List of read-only mpv properties for the stats overlay allow-list.

verifiable_in_linux_container:
Partially.

Can be verified with cargo test on Linux:
- crates/zeiler-skip parsers, using recorded JSON fixtures for AniSkip, Kitsu and TheIntroDB.
- zeiler-addon subfile.rs: gzip, BOM/UTF-16, chardetng/encoding_rs normalization on windows-1256/1251 samples, format sniffing, size cap.
- aggregate_subtitles against a local mock HTTP server.
- External-IPC line codec and event mapping, using fixture lines.
- The validate_property allow-list tables.

TS logic (subtitle ranking/dedup, next-video selection, chapter classifier, activeSegment, auto-skip state machine) can be type-checked with npm run typecheck and unit-tested if a test runner is added.

An end-to-end test of the external backend over a Unix socket is possible only if an mpv binary is installed in the container, and it would need a local test media file.

Not verifiable here:
- The embedded backend (cfg(windows) + libmpv-2.dll), Windows named pipes and the mpv OSD/keybind prompt.
- Visual UI.
- Live AniSkip / TheIntroDB / Kitsu / OpenSubtitles responses: outbound HTTPS to these hosts got CONNECT 403 from the container proxy.
